privacy: Anonymous structure review. No personal values or source URL. All letters are symbolic, not household data.
observed: C1 loan annual interest; E1 shared monthly budget; G1 home monthly appreciation; I1 portfolio monthly return (unlabelled in visible header).
E5 buyer interest plus unexplained fixed monthly increment; E6 tenant interest; D7 renter rent. G5:G7 = monthly budget minus housing spending.
B10 initial home = B5 own equity + C5 debt. Scenario label disagrees with calculated home value. No personal amounts retained.
C10:D10 initial portfolios equal first monthly contribution. E10 includes first contribution plus hardcoded own-equity minus rental-deposit difference.
B11 home grows by G1; C11:E11 = prior portfolio*(1+I1)+monthly contribution. Samples at rows 100/101 and 240/241 repeat this pattern.
F/G buyer output = home+portfolio-hardcoded initial home value+initial equity = home+portfolio-initial debt, if hardcoded initial home value is consistent.
H tenant output = portfolio+B6 own deposit equity. Since deposit=own equity+loan, this already nets tenant debt; do not subtract same debt again.

I renter output = portfolio+B7 rental deposit. Deposits and debt stay constant in sampled formulas. First row has a contribution but no home appreciation; subsequent rows apply growth then contribution.
issues: HIGH E5/F:G: unexplained buyer fixed monthly increment. If principal repayment, debt balance must decline; if operating cost, explain category. Do not declare a confirmed error before clarification.
HIGH A5/B10: scenario label and implied purchase price mismatch.
HIGH G1/I1: monthly return inputs applied monthly. Annualize as (1+r_month)^12-1, not r_month*12 for compound labels. No evidence inputs are forecasts.
MEDIUM F:G/E10: replace hardcoded initial-value and deposit-difference constants with references.
MEDIUM sampled headers/formulas: no explicit dividend/total-return, FX, tax/fee, purchase/sale friction, owner tax/maintenance, lease reset, guarantee/default assumptions.
MEDIUM B10:E11: define t=0 and month-end cashflow consistently.

proposed.fairness: Equal initial net worth W0, equal monthly available budget M after common living costs, comparable housing service, same horizon and terminal date.
proposed.initial: Buyer liquid=W0-(price-loan)-purchase costs. Tenant liquid=W0-(deposit-jeonse loan)-entry costs. Renter liquid=W0-deposit-entry costs.
proposed.recurrence: Liquid[t]=Liquid[t-1]*(1+net return[t])+M[t]-housing outflow[t]. Buyer outflow includes interest+principal+owner costs; loan[t]=loan[t-1]-principal. If contribution negative, model liquidity draw explicitly or mark infeasible.
proposed.terminal: Buyer=home-sale costs-sale taxes-debt+liquid; tenant=returned deposit-debt+liquid-exit costs; renter=returned deposit+liquid-exit costs. Show gross and liquidation adjusted values.
proposed.double_counting: Do not subtract an extra deposit opportunity-cost charge when smaller initial liquid portfolio already captures tied capital. Do not add dividends to total-return index. KRW return=(1+USD return)*(1+FX change)-1; avoid FX twice for KRW products.
proposed.sensitivity: Weak/base/strong home and portfolio paths; rates, rent/reset, holding horizon, FX and liquidity; report break-even and reversal cases, not one winner.

limits: Read-only bounded sampling: A1:Z20, A1:K12, A100:K101, A240:K241, A500:K501. Not full-grid validation. Meaning of buyer increment, actual investment instrument, total return/tax/FX basis, comparable housing service, and intervening formula exceptions remain unverified. Historical jeonse loan rate before official comparable series must be labelled a conditional assumption.
